subject.title: [Feature]: Chat background-tasks rail: eager detection badge + live tool activity on task rows

question: Should persisted tool-use count and last-tool metadata become part of OpenClaw’s task summary contract, or should this follow-up be limited to eager badge detection and elapsed duration?
rationale: Eager loading directly resolves the confirmed discoverability gap, while durable activity fields expand the stored data model and gateway-visible product contract and therefore require explicit maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Adopt registry activity
options.body: Accept additive persisted activity fields after the linked PR proves schema upgrades and every task summary and event path.

options.title: Narrow the follow-up
options.body: Land eager snapshot loading and elapsed duration while deferring durable tool activity to a broader observability design.

options.title: Retain status-only tasks
options.body: Decline richer activity metadata and preserve the current minimal task summary contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt registry activity
recommendation.body: Accept additive persisted activity fields after the linked PR proves schema upgrades and every task summary and event path.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and recently maintained the user-facing rail and is the strongest available owner for this product-contract choice.
